title: Cache memory and processor performance
question: Explain two ways in which cache memory can improve processor performance.
source_note: Original IB-style practice question aligned to the first-assessment-2027 Computer Science course.

markscheme.point: Cache stores frequently/recently used instructions or data close to the processor.
This reduces the need to access slower main memory.
A shorter access time reduces processor waiting/stalls.
This can increase instruction throughput / overall processing performance.

title: Operating system responsibilities
question: Describe three functions of an operating system.
source_note: Original IB-style practice question aligned to the first-assessment-2027 Computer Science course.

markscheme.point: Manages processes/CPU scheduling.
Manages memory allocation and virtual memory.
Manages files/devices/user interaction/security; award any one valid distinct function for the third mark.

title: Packet routing
question: Explain how packets can travel from a client device to a server across a network.
source_note: Original IB-style practice question aligned to the first-assessment-2027 Computer Science course.

markscheme.point: Data is divided into packets with addressing information.
Routers inspect destination information and select a next hop/path.
Different packets may take different routes.
Packets are reassembled/ordered at the destination and missing/corrupt data may be retransmitted where the protocol supports it.

title: Primary and foreign keys
question: Explain the role of primary keys and foreign keys in a relational database.
source_note: Original IB-style practice question aligned to the first-assessment-2027 Computer Science course.

markscheme.point: A primary key uniquely identifies each record in a table.
Primary-key values must be unique (and normally non-null).
A foreign key references a key in another/related table.
Foreign keys support relationships/referential integrity between tables.

title: Overfitting
question: Explain what overfitting is and describe one way it can be reduced when developing a machine-learning model.
source_note: Original question for new curriculum material. Machine learning is part of the first-assessment-2027 course.

markscheme.point: Overfitting occurs when a model learns training-data detail/noise too closely.
The model performs well on training data but generalizes poorly to unseen data.
Award for one valid mitigation such as regularization, simpler model, more representative training data, cross-validation, pruning, dropout, or early stopping.
Explains how the chosen mitigation improves generalization/reduces fitting to noise.

title: Bias in training data
question: Explain two ways biased training data can affect a machine-learning system.
source_note: Original question for new curriculum material.

markscheme.point: Training data can underrepresent/overrepresent groups or situations.
This can lead to systematically less accurate predictions for some groups/inputs.
Historical bias in labels/examples can be learned and reproduced by the model.
This can create unfair/discriminatory outcomes or unreliable decisions in deployment.

title: Decomposition
question: Describe how decomposition can help solve a complex computational problem.
source_note: Original IB-style practice question aligned to the first-assessment-2027 Computer Science course.

markscheme.point: Breaks a complex problem into smaller subproblems/modules.
Each subproblem can be designed/tested/solved more independently.
Solutions can then be combined, improving manageability/reuse/debugging.

title: Trace an algorithm
question: A program repeatedly checks each value in a list and keeps the largest value seen so far. Explain how this algorithm finds the maximum value and state one edge case that should be tested.
source_note: Original IB-style programming practice question; language-neutral for Java/Python preparation.

markscheme.point: Initializes a current maximum from a valid list value.
Compares each subsequent item with the current maximum.
Updates the current maximum whenever a larger value is found and returns it after the traversal.
States one valid edge case such as a single-item list, all equal values, all negative values, or an empty list if the specification permits it.

title: Debugging strategy
question: Explain two techniques a programmer can use to locate a logic error in a program.

markscheme.point: Identifies a valid technique such as trace table, debugger/breakpoint, logging, unit testing, or print tracing.
Explains how technique 1 reveals incorrect state/control flow/output.
Identifies a second distinct valid technique.
Explains how technique 2 helps isolate the source of the logic error.

title: Encapsulation
question: Explain how encapsulation can improve the design of an object-oriented program.
source_note: Original IB-style practice question aligned to the first-assessment-2027 Computer Science course.

markscheme.point: Encapsulation groups data/state with the methods that operate on it.
Internal representation can be hidden/restricted from direct external access.
Controlled interfaces/methods protect invariants or validate changes.
This reduces coupling and makes maintenance/testing/change safer.

title: Stack operations
question: Describe how a stack operates and explain one situation in which a stack is an appropriate data structure.
source_note: Original HL IB-style practice question aligned to the first-assessment-2027 Computer Science course.

markscheme.point: A stack follows last-in, first-out (LIFO) ordering.
Push adds an item to the top and pop removes/returns the top item.
Provides a valid use such as function calls, undo history, expression evaluation, DFS, or browser back history.
Explains why LIFO behavior matches the chosen situation.
